reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent static review against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP (retail PE view_1), radare2 6.2.0 CFG and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe; candidate source read from this worktree. No game process was executed and no runtime behavior is claimed.
review_basis: Retail 0x004AAA44 was re-disassembled, re-decompiled and re-CFG'd through the live Binary Ninja view, independently recovered with radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast. The candidate is scripts/GameNatives/mathsys/004AAA44-MathSys_Invoke21.cpp at sha256 59047f9a142c0bd55098649305f91688331055eb3cce177d7bdb1eae2967514b (recorded implementation.signature: int32_t __convention MathSys_Invoke21("regparm")(int32_t param_1, int32_t param_2, int32_t param_3, int32_t* param_4, void* param_5, void* param_6, int32_t param_7);). The evidence artifact digests are bound in this review.

retail_function.name: MathSys_Invoke21
retail_function.signature: int32_t __convention("regparm")(int32_t arg1, int32_t arg2, int32_t arg3, int32_t* arg4 @ ebp, void* arg5 @ esi, void* arg6 @ edi, int32_t arg7)
retail_function.summary: Five BN blocks (0x4AAA44-0x4AAA8E, 0x4AAAA0-0x4AAAB5, 0x4AAAB8-0x4AAAE4): copy seven dwords from [ESI+ECX*4+0x1C..+4] to [EDI+ECX*4+...], copy ECX*4 to ESI/EDI, then `jmp dword [edx*4+table]` on arg2 with cases 0-3; each case ends in the shared epilogue `mov eax,[ebp+8]; pop esi; pop edi; leave; retn` (the return is arg4[2]).

candidate_function.signature: int32_t __convention MathSys_Invoke21("regparm")(int32_t param_1, int32_t param_2, int32_t param_3, int32_t* param_4, void* param_5, void* param_6, int32_t param_7);
candidate_function.summary: MathSys_Invoke21 transcribes the seven dword copies and a default-less switch 0-3 whose cases fall into `return *arg4?`/`return arg4[2]`, but it omits the default/out-of-range arm and does not model the shared epilogue.

divergences: Indirect switch dispatch (`jmp dword [edx*4+table]`) is unresolved: radare2 sees 1 block, angr reports has_unresolved_jumps=true, and the candidate has no default arm.
Shared epilogue at the end of the third BN range is not transcribed; out-of-range arg2 falls off the switch.
Byte-indexed `[esi+ecx*4+off]`/`[edi+ecx*4+off]` addressing is rewritten as typed pointer arithmetic, which rescales the index.
candidate_comparison.statement: Divergences are listed above; by contract they keep the record at TRANSCRIBED or lower.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.detail: Retail entry 0x004AAA44 is recovered by all three tools; the address-bound implementation is scripts/GameNatives/mathsys/004AAA44-MathSys_Invoke21.cpp (sha256 59047f9a142c0bd55098649305f91688331055eb3cce177d7bdb1eae2967514b). Five BN blocks (0x4AAA44-0x4AAA8E, 0x4AAAA0-0x4AAAB5, 0x4AAAB8-0x4AAAE4): copy seven dwords from [ESI+ECX*4+0x1C..+4] to [EDI+ECX*4+...], copy ECX*4 to ESI/EDI, then `jmp dword [edx*4+table]` on arg2 with cases 0-3; each case ends in the shared epilogue `mov eax,[ebp+8]; pop esi; pop edi; leave; retn` (the return is arg4[2]). Candidate: MathSys_Invoke21 transcribes the seven dword copies and a default-less switch 0-3 whose cases fall into `return *arg4?`/`return arg4[2]`, but it omits the default/out-of-range arm and does not model the shared epilogue.

checks.name: abi_and_signature
checks.detail: Retail uses regparm plus EBP/ESI/EDI register arguments (BN: `int32_t __convention("regparm")(int32_t arg1, int32_t arg2, int32_t arg3, int32_t* arg4 @ ebp, void* arg5 @ esi, void* arg6 @ edi, int32_t arg7)`). The candidate declares the recorded 7-parameter regparm prototype but never binds arg5/arg6 to ESI/EDI or arg4 to EBP.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.detail: arg3 (ECX) indexes the copy, arg5 (ESI) is the source base and arg6 (EDI) the destination in retail; the candidate's body uses the parameter names but its pointer arithmetic (`arg5 + (arg3 << 2) + 0x1C`) does not reproduce the byte-indexed retail addressing and arg4/EBP is unused.

checks.name: control_flow_shape
checks.detail: BN reports 5 blocks / 0 edges plus three ranges (main body, jump-table island, shared epilogue); radare2 stops at the indirect jump and reports 1 block, and angr CFGFast marks the function inconclusive with has_unresolved_jumps=true. The indirect `jmp dword [edx*4 + table]` dispatch is not resolved statically by either CFG tool.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.detail: No calls in either; the dispatch is an indirect jump in both.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.detail: The seven offsets 0x1C/0x18/0x14/0x10/0xC/8/4 and the ×4 index scaling match.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.detail: Retail copies `[esi+ecx*4+off]` to `[edi+ecx*4+off]` byte-addressed; the candidate's `arg5 + (arg3 << 2) + 0x1C` is pointer arithmetic on the parameter type, which rescales the offset. The destination base also does not carry the ECX*4 adjustment the retail code applies to EDI.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.detail: Retail's shared epilogue returns [EBP+8] (arg4[2]) from every case; the candidate's `return arg4[2]` relies on the decompiler's `*arg4;` dead load and has no default arm, so an out-of-range arg2 falls off the function.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports "int32_t __convention("regparm")(int32_t arg1, int32_t arg2, int32_t arg3, int32_t* arg4 @ ebp, void* arg5 @ esi, void* arg6 @ edi, int32_t arg7)" at 0x004AAA44; radare2 recovers "fcn.004aaa44 ();". Both tools place the entry at 0x004AAA44 and agree on the stack/register word count and cleanup; the difference is the level of type/argument-name detail, not the call frame. Candidate declaration: int32_t __convention MathSys_Invoke21("regparm")(int32_t param_1, int32_t param_2, int32_t param_3, int32_t* param_4, void* param_5, void* param_6, int32_t param_7);. The candidate declaration is separately recorded as divergent below and does not satisfy the retail ABI.

limitations: No game process was executed; this review is static (live Binary Ninja, radare2 CFG, angr CFGFast) plus the candidate source.
The candidate defines MathSys_Invoke21; the catalog name is a harvest label.
BN's three ranges total 140 bytes while the block table covers 138; the 2-byte difference is an uncovered BN block boundary, not candidate evidence.
